faqs.a: While theoretically possible, the mathematical probability is virtually zero. To have a 50% chance of a single collision, you would need to generate over 2.71 quintillion UUIDs (2,710,000,000,000,000,000).

faqs.q: Is UUID case-sensitive in databases?
faqs.a: Under RFC 4122, UUIDs are formally specified in lowercase hexadecimal. However, most modern databases (PostgreSQL uuid type, SQL Server UNIQUEIDENTIFIER) treat UUID strings as case-insensitive 16-byte binary integers.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a UUID and a GUID?
faqs.a: They refer to the exact same 128-bit identifier standard. UUID is the official IETF/ISO term, while GUID is the terminology popularized by Microsoft in Windows and .NET.

faqs.q: Are UUIDs safe to use as primary keys in relational databases?
faqs.a: Yes, but for B-tree index performance on extremely high-write database tables, random UUID v4 can cause index fragmentation. Modern systems often use UUID v7 (time-ordered random) or store UUID v4 in binary(16) format to optimize storage.
